correctness.rationale: Exact series resistance on a tree reduces the all-pairs objective to the maximum sum of two reciprocal conductances. Positive normalization gives the equivalent convex scalar cost minimization on a pair-constrained region. Case analysis at one-half, equality characterization of every cost lower bound, strict convexity of f_j and a unique possible majority price prove the exact global formula and uniqueness including m=2 and equality. The executable independently checks budget, grounded-network effective resistance, finite dual feasible grids, and a nonuniform rational example. The checker is not the infinite proof.

originality.rationale: The inspected 2006 and 2008 Ghosh–Boyd–Saberi primary texts explicitly introduce the all-pairs maximum-effective-resistance objective but supply a general convex/SDP formulation rather than the all-dimension, arbitrary-positive-price star solution. The Suliman–Weinstein primary full text minimizes the maximum over network EDGES, not all pairs of vertices; its optimization is logically different even on stars. Earlier records for conductance allocation on stars in the local history instead optimize Laplacian spectral gap or observability. Search results in published research and published-finding corpus did not identify an equivalent majority-price star classification. This is a narrowly scoped self-review subject to residual risk, not universal literature certification.
residual_risks: A mathematically equivalent theorem in historical network-sizing or minimax resource-allocation literature may escape title/semantic search.

value.rationale: The worst-pair effective-resistance diameter is a motivated design objective explicitly proposed in GBS06 and GBS08. Determining its globally optimal priced conductance on all positive-cost stars exposes a sharp aggregate price dominance boundary and a counterintuitive region where heterogeneous prices have no effect on the unique uniform allocation. It gives closed-form design and optimal-value formulas for any number of leaves, unlike a tiny unmotivated finite calculation. Limitation: no analogous arbitrary-tree or nonlinear-price claim.
